person.canonical_name_en: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies

activity.notes: The Bourbon monarchy was restored in Naples later in 1799 after the fall of the Neapolitan Republic. Ferdinand IV again ruled the Kingdom of Naples until the French invasion of 1806 drove him to Sicily and Napoleon transferred the Neapolitan crown to his own dynasty. ATLAS preserves this as a second, interrupted Neapolitan reign.

sources.title: Ferdinando I di Borbone già IV come re di Napoli e III come re di Sicilia — Treccani
sources.citation_text: Treccani identifies Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies as formerly Ferdinand IV of Naples and Ferdinand III of Sicily, succeeding in 1759, losing Naples in 1799, regaining it, losing Naples again in 1806, recovering it in 1815, and creating the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1816.

sources.title: FERDINANDO I di Borbone, re delle Due Sicilie — Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani, Treccani
sources.citation_text: The Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani confirms Ferdinand's accession to the Neapolitan and Sicilian crowns in 1759 and his later identity as Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies.
